title: OKC-SFT Post-Mortem: Reducing the Hallucination Rate of Industrial Diagnostic Large Models from 34.4% to 15.6%
subtitle: A Complete Practice of Supervised Fine-Tuning on Operation Knowledge Chains for Anomaly Handling in Air Separation Units
markdown: > This article reviews the complete practice of my first-author paper, OKC-SFT: a structured fine-tuning method for operational commands in air separation unit anomaly handling. The paper has been submitted to CAC 2026, and the dataset is open-sourced on GitHub (CC BY 4.0). All numbers in the text are reproducible. ## 1. Problem: Industrial Scenarios Cannot Tolerate Hallucinations Air separation units (ASUs) are core equipment in process industries. In abnormal operating conditions, operators need executable handling instructions. When asked questions like "What should be done when the crude argon tower experiences nitrogen blockage?", general large language models often provide answers that sound professional but are fundamentally incorrect upon closer inspection: they fabricate non-existent valve identifiers, reverse the handling sequence, and omit safety boundaries that require an emergency shutdown. In chat scenarios, hallucinations are user experience issues; in industrial handling scenarios, hallucinations are safety incidents. This project addresses only one thing: ensuring that every handling instruction output by the fine-tuned model is executable, verifiable, and bounded. ## 2. Method: Explicitly Formalizing Handling Logic into a Six-Element Chain Analysis of the response habits of excellent operators reveals that qualified handling instructions naturally follow a complete logical chain. We explicitly formalize this as the Operation Knowledge Chain (OKC) six elements, requiring the model to output all six fields for every response: | Field | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | Diagnosis | Determine the abnormal state and its severity | | Evidence | Provide process variables, equipment status, and measured values that support the judgment | | Possible Causes | Explain the causal mechanism and potential fault sources | | Operation Suggestions | Executable operational steps | | Verification Indices | Monitoring variables and recovery criteria after operations | | Safety Notes | When to decelerate, stop, or escalate reporting | Core idea: Hallucinations are most likely to occur where the model "freely improvises." The six-field structure anchors every step of the response into mandatory slots, leaving the model no room for arbitrary improvisation. If any field is missing, it becomes immediately visible at the evaluation stage. ## 3. Data: 611 structured samples and 858 unstructured baselines To demonstrate that the gain stems from structure rather than data volume, we constructed two sets of training data for comparison, both in the scenario of nitrogen plugging in a crude argon tower (nitrogen_plugging): | Dataset | Sample Count | Format | Role | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | okc_sft_train.jsonl | 611 | Six-field structured output | Experimental group | | qa_sft_train.jsonl | 858 | Conventional Q&A output | Baseline group | | test_set.jsonl | 61 | Balanced distribution across six task types | Evaluation set | Three design details are worth noting: 1. **Full-field output**. For every sample in OKC-SFT, regardless of question type, the output must contain all six fields. For a question like 'What does the tag AI705 mean?', the model must still traverse the full chain from diagnosis to risk boundaries, making the structure a muscle memory. 2. **Traceable sources**. Each sample's metadata includes a `source_trace`, marking which source Q&A and which knowledge chain item it originated from, enabling item-by-item tracing if data issues arise. 3. **Evaluation set includes key points**. The test set does not contain the full text of standard answers, but only `expected_key_points` (expected key points), such as 'AI705 represents crude argon purity; a continuous decline is the core early warning signal for nitrogen blockage', leaving an interface for automated evaluation. ## 4. Evaluation: A complete loop composed of three metrics There is no existing benchmark for industrial Q&A, so we built our own evaluation loop around three metrics: | Metric | Meaning | Target Direction | | --- | --- | --- | | Full-field output rate | Whether the output contains all six fields | Higher is better | | Key point coverage rate | The proportion of `expected_key_points` hit | Higher is better | | Hallucination rate | The proportion of fabricated tags, incorrect operations, or fictional mechanisms in the output | Lower is better | The base model is Qwen2.5-7B, fine-tuned with LoRA. First, train the baseline group and run one round of evaluation, then train the experimental group and run the same evaluation. Both rounds use the identical test set and scoring criteria to ensure fair comparison. ## 5. Results | Metric | QA-SFT Baseline (858 samples) | OKC-SFT (611 samples) | | --- | --- | --- | | Hallucination Rate | 34.4% | **15.6%** | | Structural Integrity Rate | No structural constraints | 99.8% | | Key Point Coverage | Lower than the experimental group | 0.7378 | Three points worth emphasizing: 1. **Less structured data won over more unstructured data**. 611 against 858, with the hallucination rate dropping by more than half, indicating that the gain comes from the structural constraints themselves. 2. **Structural integrity rate near perfect** indicates that the six-field format has been stably learned by the model, and format constraints are realized at zero cost. 3. **A hallucination rate of 15.6% is still substandard**. Industrial deployment still requires retrieval-augmented generation and human review as fallbacks, and the paper honestly discusses this point. ## VI. Experience Summary 1. **Structure is constraint**. The most direct way to suppress hallucinations is to narrow the output space to mandatory fill-in slots, which is much cheaper than piling up data or parameters. 2. **Evaluation before training**. The expected_key_points and scoring criteria were defined before training the model, ensuring that all subsequent iterations have a unified benchmark, avoiding development based on 'feeling improved'. 3. **Small-scale vertical fine-tuning is feasible**. 611 high-quality samples are sufficient for a 7B model to learn an answer paradigm for an industrial scenario, provided that the format and source of each sample are strictly controlled. 4. **Traceability has saved lives.** Some erroneous samples identified during data review were corrected by tracing them back to their source Q&A pairs one by one using source_trace. Without this mechanism, we would have had to re-read the entire dataset. 5. **Honesty about residual hallucinations.** Reporting 15.6% in the paper is more valuable than packaging it as 0%; it directly defines the goals for the next phase (RAG + review pipeline). ## 7. Open Source Resources - Dataset: [OKC-SFT-Dataset](https://github.com/Xplore-LAB/OKC-SFT-Dataset) (CC BY 4.0), containing all training, baseline, and test data - Compatible with LLaMA-Factory; simply copy into the data directory to start training - Paper: Submitted to CAC 2026, currently validated only in a single scenario (Nitrogen Clog), with multi-scenario expansion in progress Feel free to raise issues on GitHub for discussion.
